contentSummary: This subtopic provides insights in understanding political parties and how they operate. It further outlines how leaders are chosen and how political parties interact with citizens in society. Through this sub topic learner will learn how political parties provide a platform for citizens to participate in decision-making process. Specific Competence Learners to: Analyse the Organisation and Structure of a Political Party Learning ActivitiesDescribing a political party A political partyA political party is a group of citizens who organize themselves with a common value, ideas and a goal towards forming government. A political party represents an alternative government in a country. Political parties originate from different aspects of our communities.The following are some of the factors that lead to the formation of political parties: Ideological differences: disagreements over ideology, principles and policies can lead to the formation of new parties. Teaching Module3 Economic interests: disagreements over economic policies and interests can lead to party formation Charismatic leaders: individuals with persuasive and compelling attitudes can lead others in the formation of a political party Human nature (inborn differences): by nature, people differ in the way they understand and look at issues of life. Therefore, differences in opinion lead people to form political parties Religious and communal sentiments: some people form political parties according to their religious beliefs Regional and geographic interests: parties may form to represent the interests of specific regions or geographic areas. For example, in the United States of America, the Republican Party initially represented the interests of the Northern states, while the Democratic Party, the Southern states Social and cultural issues: parties may form around social and cultural issues such as slavery, civil rights or immigration Historical events and crises: major historical events such as wars, economic depressions or social unrest may lead to the formation of parties. Learning ActivitiesDifferentiating between ruling party and an opposition party Differences between the ruling and opposition partiesa. Ruling party The ruling party is the political party which governs a country after winning elections and holds the governing power. It forms the executive arm of government (cabinet) headed by the president which is responsible for policy formulation and implementation. In the legislature, the ruling party initiates laws through public bills in line with its vision and development goals as enshrined in the party manifesto. It mobilises citizens to support national initiatives and government programmes.b. Opposition party An opposition political party is any political party which is not in government but works to provide checks and balances on the ruling party. This is done by questioning the actions, policies and decisions of government in power. It ensures that the government remains answerable to the citizens by holding government accountable for its actions It provides a healthy democracy by ensuring that government is accountable, transparent and responsive to the needs of the citizens. It presents alternative policies and programmes for development purposes and stands as an alternative government. It educates the public on important national and international issues Opposition political parties raise public debates that in turn force government consider popular concerns in the interest of the public Learning ActivitiesOutlining the structure of a political party (National Executive Committee, Provincial Executive Committee, District Executive Committee, Constituency Committee, Sections and Branches) Functions of a political party Selection or nomination of political personal Formation of public policies Conducting and criticism of government Political education. International between people and government Development and maintenance of s sense of national unity Coordinating the branches of government Making it possible for the electorate to function in an organized and effective manner. Framing of political issue for the people Selection of candidates during elections Serving as agencies of civic education Parties develop a sense of national unity Formulate party policies They permit the electorate to function They seek to control government They minimize the crushes of economic interests for the demand of various economic groups find expressions in party platforms. Teaching Module7 Learning ActivitiesDramatising a political campaign activity (meeting) A political party campaign is a selling of political ideas to the public in order to win the support of the public. it involves the dissemination of political party message to the public through rallies, debates, door to door canvasing, social media engangements and town hall meetings every political party has rights to disseminate information about its policies and idiologies as a means towards winning people’s trust to gain the votes The History of Political Party System in ZambiaSince independence Zambia’s political party system has changed from multiparty to one party and back to multiparty as illustrated in the table below:Party SystemPeriod Major Political Parties Party in PowerMulti-Party System 1964 to1972 - United National Independence Party (UNIP)- African national Congress (ANC)- United Progressive Party (UPP)United National Independence Party (UNIP)One-Party System 1973 to 1991 United National Independence Party (UNIP) United National Independence Party (UNIP)Multi-Party System 1991 to Date - Movement for Multiparty De-mocracy (MMD)- United National Independence Party (UNIP)- Patriotic Front (PF)- United Party for National Devel-opment (UPND) MMD (1991 to 2011)PF (2011 to 2021)UPND (2021 to ...) contentSummary: Zambia operates through both Local and Central Government systems. Local government is normally the decentralised system where power to govern is given to local authorities or councils to provide certain services to the communities at district level. Here learners will be given an opportunity to acquire more knowledge and competencies concerning the past and present trends in local authorities in Zambia. Before independence, the British Colonial administration ruled through tradition-al leaders or native authorities. Native authorities assisted the colonial government in collecting taxes, issuing licences and presiding over civil cases. After independence, Zambia enacted the Local Government Act Number 69 of 1965 which created four types of councils; City Councils, Municipal Councils Township Councils and Rural Councils. In 1980, the Local government and Decentralisation Act was enacted which placed all council under the control of District Governors In 1991, the Local Government and Decentralisation Act of 1980 was amended creating the current three types of autonomous councils; City (for cities), Munic-ipal (For Provincial Headquarters and other big towns) and District Councils (for small towns or districts). The 2019 Local Government Act outlines the three main types of Local Councils based on the size and status of the area they govern. The three are City councils, Municipal Councils and Town Councils. Learning ActivitiesExamining the structure of the local councils (city council, municipal council and town council) Under the current Local Government Act, City and Municipal Councils are headed by Mayors while District Councils are administered by Council Chairpersons together with Ward Councillors as Decision Makers. The administrative functions of the City and Municipal Councils are placed under the Town Clerk while the Town Councils are under the Council Secretary working with Directors of various Departments. THE STRUCTURE OF LOCAL COUNCILSCOUNCIL TYPEPOLITICAL HEAD (For Decision Making) ADMINISTARTIVE HEAD (For Implementing Programmes)City Councils Mayor working with ward councillors Town Clerk working with Directors of Departments Municipal CouncilsMayor working with ward councillors Town Clerk working with Directors of DepartmentsTown Councils Council Chairperson working with ward councillors Council Secretary working with Directors of Departments Local councils perform the following functions: zMaking By-Laws zProviding clean and safe water to communities zProviding accommodation and allocating plots for development zEnsuring a clean environment and pollution control zAllocating land for and maintaining graveyards zAwarding trading licences to business persons Teaching Module19 zMaintaining township roads and streets zBuilding and maintaining trading places such as markets zProviding street lighting zControlling the movement of livestock to and from the district zControlling drainage and sewage disposal zCity and town planning zProviding recreation facilities such as swimming pools and play parks zCollecting various kinds of levies, rates and rentals zProviding health facilities and controlling epidemics in communities zProviding fire-fighting services zPromoting local tourism Learning ActivitiesIdentifying sources of revenue for Local Government To undertake daily operations, local councils need to raise enough revenue. The most common ways by which councils raise funds are: zBusiness levies from business persons in the district zGrants from government such as the Equalisation Fund zPersonal levies paid by workers annually to the council zIssuance of Trading Licences zLocal revenue raising measures through such means as barriers, lodges, land rates, animal and crop levy among others zConstituency Development Fund for service delivery to constituencies Expected Standard: Functions of Local Government examined appropriately One of the key functions of the local councils is to ensure environmental care and sanitation. This is mostly done through the following means: Cleaning public surroundings Tree planting in designated areas Providing and managing toilets in public places Providing rubbish bins in public places Developing and managing dumpsites Sewer and drainage control Sweeping of public places Provision of clean water and sanitation Learning ActivitiesIdentifying institutions and organisations that care for the environment Learning Environmwent Setup: This activity can be conducted from the natural environment through visiting institutions Teaching and Learning materials: Chart showing institutions helping in environmental care.Suggested Teaching Methods: Field VisitActivity Process zTake learners to a nearby organisation involved in environmental care such as the Zambia Environmental Management Agency (ZEMA), Health Centre, the council or any other Civil Society Organisation. z Learners to discuss what they learnt during the field trip and make presentations based on the discussions Taking care of the environment is an important activity which cannot be left to the local authorities alone. Other institutions and organisations can contribute significantly towards environmental care. These may include the following: zZambia Environmental Management Agency (ZEMA) zLine Government Ministries zCivil Society (CSOs) involved in environmental Management zNone Governmental Organisations (NGOs) committed to environmental care zSchools zReligious bodies zHouseholds and Communities Expected Standard: Environment cared for accordingly This subtopic highlights the roles played by traditional leaders in the governance of a country. Through this topic, learners will be made to understand the composition and functions of the House of Chiefs in Zambia. Specific Competence Learners to: Demonstrate understanding of the role of traditional rulers in the governance of the country Traditional leadership has been at the core of Zambia’s governance from pre-colonial, colonial and post-colonial eras. In pre-colonial era, traditional leaders were the only known leaders in the Zambian societies. The colonial administration practiced indirect rule by using traditional leadership to govern societies. Currently Zambia has a total of 288 Chiefs who play a significant role in the governance of a nation. They influence and motivate their subjects to achieve common goals and maintain order and harmony in communities. Traditional leaders play various roles in their communities which in-clude: zproviding spiritual guidance to their subjects zto preside over cultural, judicial and administrative activities in the chiefdoms. zTo resolve conflict among subjects zTo spearhead economic and social development in the community. zTo provide advice to political and religious leaders in society. zThey lobby for and spearhead developmental projects for their chiefdoms zThey are custodians of traditional leadership, customs and traditional land in their chiefdoms Article 169 of the Constitution of Zambia provides that there is established a House of Chiefs which shall consist of five chiefs from each province, elected by the chiefs in a Province, as prescribed.According to Article 169 Clause 5 of the Constitution, the functions of the House of Chiefs are to:(a) consider and discuss a Bill relating to custom or tradition referred to it by the President, before the Bill is introduced into the National Assembly;(b) initiate, discuss and make recommendations to the National Assembly regarding socio-economic development in the province;(c) initiate, discuss and decide on matters relating to customary law and practice;(d) initiate, discuss and make recommendations to a local authority regarding the welfare of communities in a local authority;(e) make proposals on areas in customary law that require codification;(f) advise the Government on traditional and customary matters; and(g) perform other functions as prescribed. contentSummary: The concept money zMoney is anything of value used to buy goods and to pay for services. It is a medium of exchange that is agreed upon or accepted to be used by society. zIn ancient times people used to exchange one item for another. That was referred to as barter system. For example, people would use salt to exchange with gold. zIt was later realized that barter system alone could not make trade easy because some article that were used in trade were very heavy and sometimes it was difficult to harmonise the article with the value of something that someone wanted. zWith the rise in civilization, bank notes and coins were introduced to easy transactions. zThe value of money is the amount of goods and services it buys or pays for. This means that the price is the value of the commodities and services expressed in monetary form. zThe general increase in the price of goods and services reduces the purchasing power of money leading to inflation. Learning Activities Describing the characteristics of money The following are some of the main characteristics of money: zPortability- meaning money should be easy to carry. zDurability- meaning that money should last for a long time without being damaged. zDivisibility- Meaning that it must be easy to divide money into smaller units. zUniformity- This means that unit of money should be uniform in terms of design. zAcceptability- meaning that money must be widely agreed upon and accepted by people as a means of exchange. z Scarcity- Money should not be easy to find. Learning ActivitiesAnalysing the Functions of Money The functions of money are: Medium of exchange: it enables people to buy one item which they can later sell to get what they want. Store of value: People can convert their wealth into money. Measure of value or unit of account: Money is used as a standard to quantify the value of goods and services. Means of deferred payment: getting commodities and pay later. Teaching Module35 zDemand is the ability and willingness of people to pay for goods and services. zSupply is the availability of goods and services on the market. zThe law of demand and supply explains the interaction between the two concepts. zThis law states that the price of the product will go down if the supply increases or the demand for the product is low. On the contrary, the price of the product will go up if the supply decreases or if the demand for the product is high. zSometimes the demand can match the supply. This is called equilibrium point. Here, the price of the goods seems to be fair to both the customers and the sellers. zHigh Demand + Low Supply= High Price zLow Demand + High Supply= Low Price zModerate Demand + Moderate Supply= Fair Price (equilibrium) zHigh Demand + High Supply= High Price (exception to the law of demand and supply) Money Laundering zMoney laundering means making money which has been acquired illegally look clean. This is done by passing illegally acquired money through a legitimate business or bank account in order to disguise its illegal origins. Money laundering activities z Money laundering activities include; Fraud, concealment or deception, theft, counterfeiting, collusion, forgery, false pretence among others. zPeople who practice money laundering are those involved in drug trafficking, bribery, smuggling, terrorism and sell of illegal arms among others.Effects of Money Laundering zLeads to an increase in corruption and crime. zUndermines national revenue collection zDamages the integrity of the country zundermines democracy and the rule of law. zAffects direct foreign investment Evaluating business opportunities involves doing a thorough analysis of different factors to establish their potential and check if they match with the goals and resources. How to Evaluate Business Opportunities: Certain steps have to be followed to help someone to evaluate business opportunities. The following are some of the step guides: zAlignment with goals. Ensure the opportunity is in line with your objectives, values and mission. zMarket demand. Make a survey of the market to determine if there is a genuine demand for the product or service zCompetitive landscape. Analyse the competition so that you understand the market’s saturation and to see the potential to engage in something different zTarget audience. Identify the target audience and their needs and preferences. zMarket size and growth. Make an estimate of the market size, growth potential and trends. zBarriers to entry. Assess the ease or difficulty of entering the market, including regulatory requirements, competition and compliance. zRevenue potential. Estimate the potential revenue and profit margins. This subtopic looks at saving and its importance. It also describes different ways of saving. Saving can be described as an act of setting aside a portion of one’s income or resources for future use and not spent immediately. Saving money is important because it ensures financial security and a peace of mind. Through this topic learners will learn the different ways of saving money and why saving is important. Saving provides individuals, households, businesses and the broader economy with a number of significant benefits. Some of the reasons why saving is significant are that it provides: Financial Security: Saving provides a safety net for unforeseen expenses, emergencies and financial shock. This reduces financial stress and anxiety. Investment or Wealth Creation: By putting aside part of one’s income, individuals can accumulate and grow wealth over time for use to achieve long- term financial goals. Independence: Saving give individuals financial independence. That enables them to make choices about their lives, careers and future. Reduced Debt: Saving can help individuals reduce their debt burden by providing a source of funds for debt repayment. Increased Financial Flexibility: Saving provides with financial flexibility to take advantage of new opportunities such investing in education or starting anew business. Improved Financial literacy: It helps individuals develop good financial habits and improve their financial literacy. This can lead to better financial decision-making and a stable financial future. The following are ways of saving: Teaching Module41 zPiggy Bank: keeping of money in a tin or box zVillage Banking: Saving money in groups and gaining interest zChilimba: Putting money together and giving it to one person monthly zMobile Banking: Keeping money through a mobile money systems zBank Accounts: Keeping money in the bank Spending is when money is used to buy or pay for goods and services. People spend money in different ways, depending on their needs and wants. This subtopic focuses on being prudent about spending money. Specific Competences Learners to: exhibit Personal Financial Management Learning ActivitiesExploring the significance of practicing personal finance management zPersonal finance management is about making smart choices with money. zBudgeting, saving, investing, and spending responsibly are all part of Personal finance management. zMoney managing can help avoid problems in the future, such as running out of money or not having enough for important things; and be financially prepared for the future. Teaching Module43 Learning ActivitiesDemonstrating how to manage their Finances zFinancial management is key when to comes to spending money. It is important to balance between needs and wants. zSaving money for future goals or emergencies is just as important as enjoying the present. zCreating a budget helps to prioritize spending and saving. zSetting goals and saving money helps persons to be financially prepared for the future.
